IVX FULL RORK INDEPENDENCE MIGRATION — ZERO-DOWNTIME EXECUTION

OWNER DIRECTIVE

IVXHolding, IVX IA Chat, the autonomous senior-developer worker, repositories, cloud services, domains, databases, credentials, deployment infrastructure, and source code are owner-controlled.

The objective is to remove every Rork dependency while preserving all existing IVX functionality.

Do not:
- Delete Rork integrations before replacements are live.
- Break production.
- Disable IVX IA Chat.
- Disable the autonomous worker.
- Reset or replace the current IVX codebase.
- Rewrite working systems unnecessarily.
- Remove secrets without first binding their replacements.
- claim completion without runtime evidence.

Use a staged migration with rollback protection.

==================================================
PHASE 1 — COMPLETE DEPENDENCY INVENTORY
==================================================

Scan the entire repository and runtime configuration for:

- RORK
- rork
- EXPO_PUBLIC_RORK_*
- Rork API URLs
- Rork authentication URLs
- Rork function URLs
- Rork toolkit URLs
- Rork app keys
- Rork proxy calls
- Rork Git Data API usage
- Rork sandbox assumptions
- .rork directory dependencies
- Rork-specific build scripts
- Rork-specific deployment commands
- Rork-hosted assets
- Rork-only secrets
- Rork-only callbacks or webhooks

Produce a dependency table containing:

- Dependency
- File or configuration location
- Current purpose
- Direct replacement
- Migration risk
- Rollback method
- Verification test

Do not remove anything during the inventory phase.

==================================================
PHASE 2 — CREATE AN INDEPENDENT DEVELOPMENT ENVIRONMENT
==================================================

Create and verify a complete development setup outside Rork.

Required:

- Repository can be cloned directly from GitHub.
- Dependencies install successfully.
- Backend starts locally.
- Expo/mobile app starts locally.
- IVX IA Chat works locally.
- Autonomous worker starts locally.
- Supabase connects directly.
- Vercel AI Gateway connects directly.
- Render configuration is documented.
- Environment variables are loaded from owner-controlled configuration.
- Tests run without the Rork sandbox.

Create:

- README-independent-development.md
- .env.example with variable names only
- local startup scripts
- test scripts
- build scripts
- deployment instructions
- troubleshooting instructions

Never expose secret values.

==================================================
PHASE 3 — REPLACE RORK ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES
==================================================

Replace every Rork-specific variable with an IVX-owned variable.

Examples:

EXPO_PUBLIC_RORK_API_BASE_URL
→ EXPO_PUBLIC_IVX_API_BASE_URL

EXPO_PUBLIC_RORK_AUTH_URL
→ EXPO_PUBLIC_IVX_AUTH_URL

EXPO_PUBLIC_RORK_FUNCTIONS_URL
→ EXPO_PUBLIC_IVX_FUNCTIONS_URL

EXPO_PUBLIC_RORK_TOOLKIT_URL
→ direct IVX or provider endpoint

EXPO_PUBLIC_RORK_APP_KEY
→ remove if unnecessary or replace with an IVX-owned application identifier

EXPO_PUBLIC_RORK_TOOLKIT_SECRET_KEY
→ server-side owner-controlled secret only; never expose in Expo public variables

Requirements:

- Add new IVX variables first.
- Support temporary dual-read compatibility.
- Prefer IVX variables.
- Fall back to old Rork variables only during migration.
- Verify production with IVX variables.
- Remove fallback only after all tests pass.

Do not place secrets in EXPO_PUBLIC_* variables.

==================================================
PHASE 4 — REPLACE RORK PROXY AND TOOLKIT CALLS
==================================================

For every Rork proxy or toolkit call:

1. Identify the actual provider or service.
2. Replace the proxy with a direct owner-controlled integration.
3. Preserve authentication, timeouts, retries, logging, and error handling.
4. Add tests for the replacement.
5. Verify responses match or improve upon current behavior.

Direct services should include, where applicable:

- GitHub API
- Render API
- Supabase
- Vercel AI Gateway
- OpenAI-compatible provider interfaces
- IVX-owned backend endpoints
- Expo/EAS
- Owner-controlled authentication endpoints

No runtime request should depend on rork.com or Rork infrastructure after migration.

==================================================
PHASE 5 — INDEPENDENT GITHUB CI/CD
==================================================

Create GitHub Actions workflows owned by the repository.

Required workflows:

1. Pull Request QA
- install
- TypeScript
- lint
- unit tests
- integration tests
- security checks
- build validation

2. Main Deployment
- run full QA
- deploy backend to Render
- wait for deployment
- verify /health
- verify /version
- verify production SHA equals GitHub SHA

3. Mobile Build
- build Android
- build iOS
- retain build artifacts
- support EAS or an independent native build pipeline

4. Autonomous Worker QA
- test task creation
- test code modification
- test commit
- test PR creation
- test approval path
- test merge
- test deployment
- test production verification
- test ledger evidence

GitHub Actions must run without Rork APIs.

==================================================
PHASE 6 — INDEPENDENT MOBILE RELEASE PIPELINE
==================================================

Replace Expo Go-only dependence with owner-controlled production builds.

Required:

- Configure EAS under the owner-controlled Expo account, or create native build pipelines.
- Generate signed Android App Bundle.
- Generate signed iOS archive.
- Verify app launches independently of Rork.
- Verify API configuration points to IVX domains.
- Verify authentication.
- Verify IVX IA Chat.
- Verify autonomous status interfaces.
- Verify production push configuration where applicable.
- Prepare App Store Connect build.
- Prepare Google Play internal-testing build.

Do not remove Expo Go development support until standalone builds work.

==================================================
PHASE 7 — PRESERVE IVX IA CHAT
==================================================

IVX IA Chat must continue working throughout migration.

Verify:

- Identity responses.
- Math responses.
- Real AI provider responses.
- Conversation persistence.
- Owner authentication.
- Public chat.
- Private chat.
- Timeouts.
- Error handling.
- Health status.
- Provider status.
- No Rork fallback.
- No Rork proxy.
- No request to rork.com.

Required final evidence:

- request URL
- provider used
- response status
- latency
- production commit
- direct dependency path

==================================================
PHASE 8 — PRESERVE AUTONOMOUS SENIOR-DEVELOPER WORKER
==================================================

The autonomous worker must remain operational.

Verify the complete owner-controlled chain:

Owner instruction
→ IVX task record
→ autonomous analysis
→ code change
→ tests
→ commit
→ GitHub PR
→ approval
→ merge
→ Render deploy
→ health verification
→ SHA parity
→ evidence ledger
→ result returned to IVX IA Chat

Requirements:

- No Rork Git Data API.
- No Rork sandbox.
- No Rork deployment command.
- No Rork proxy.
- No manual recovery caused by removing Rork.
- Credentials must load from existing owner-controlled runtime variables.
- Do not ask the owner to recreate credentials unless runtime evidence proves they are missing, revoked, expired, deleted, or returning 401/403.

==================================================
PHASE 9 — PARALLEL PRODUCTION VALIDATION
==================================================

Before removing Rork compatibility:

Run both paths temporarily:

- Existing path
- New independent IVX path

Compare:

- API responses
- AI responses
- authentication
- database writes
- autonomous task execution
- commits
- PR creation
- deployments
- production health
- SHA parity
- audit logs

The independent IVX path must complete at least:

- 10 successful IVX IA Chat requests
- 3 successful real autonomous engineering tasks
- 3 successful deployments
- 3 successful production verifications
- 1 Android production build
- 1 iOS production build

No Rork dependency may be used during these validation runs.

==================================================
PHASE 10 — CUTOVER
==================================================

Only after all previous phases pass:

1. Make IVX-owned endpoints the only active endpoints.
2. Disable Rork fallback variables.
3. Remove Rork proxy calls.
4. Remove Rork deployment integrations.
5. Remove Rork build integrations.
6. Remove unused Rork environment variables.
7. Remove .rork runtime dependencies.
8. Preserve only historical files if legally or operationally required.
9. Deploy.
10. Verify production.

Use feature flags or reversible commits so rollback is possible.

==================================================
PHASE 11 — FINAL RORK REMOVAL AUDIT
==================================================

Run repository and runtime searches.

Required final results:

- 0 active Rork API calls
- 0 Rork authentication dependencies
- 0 Rork function dependencies
- 0 Rork toolkit dependencies
- 0 Rork deployment dependencies
- 0 Rork build dependencies
- 0 Rork runtime environment variables
- 0 Rork sandbox requirements
- 0 Rork Git Data API dependencies
- 0 production requests to Rork-controlled domains

Historical documentation references must be clearly marked historical and must not affect runtime.

==================================================
FINAL ACCEPTANCE EVIDENCE
==================================================

Return evidence only:

- GitHub repository URL
- GitHub HEAD SHA
- Production SHA
- SHA parity
- GitHub Actions workflow runs
- Render deployment ID
- Production health result
- Production version result
- IVX IA Chat direct-provider tests
- Autonomous worker end-to-end task evidence
- Android build ID
- iOS build ID
- Direct service endpoint inventory
- Rork dependency scan results
- Remaining Rork references, if any
- Rollback commit
- Final status

Completion requires:

✓ IVX runs outside Rork.
✓ IVX can be developed outside Rork.
✓ IVX can be tested outside Rork.
✓ IVX can be deployed outside Rork.
✓ IVX IA Chat works without Rork.
✓ Autonomous senior-developer worker works without Rork.
✓ GitHub CI/CD works without Rork.
✓ Mobile builds work without Rork.
✓ Owner-controlled services and credentials are used.
✓ No active production dependency remains on Rork.
✓ No production crash or functionality reversal occurred.

Do not report “100% independent” until every acceptance item is supported by real runtime evidence.
